### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via installCommentAccessHooks (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **61** of **218** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **157** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **157**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **102** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b27c6b3d4b14302b48179e29c4c85fbc9b75e87c` — the merge of head `dde4c9f4b208244fc75c4a8b85869389f8718154` into base `0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b27c6b3d4b14302b48179e29c4c85fbc9b75e87c && git checkout b27c6b3d4b14302b48179e29c4c85fbc9b75e87c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd dde4c9f4b208244fc75c4a8b85869389f8718154 && git checkout -B drift-repro 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd && git merge --no-ff dde4c9f4b208244fc75c4a8b85869389f8718154

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 0b2b309cb4ce737888f7280b896f7bcece9315bd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dde4c9f4b208244fc75c4a8b85869389f8718154`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-access-hooks.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/objects/sys-comment.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-plugin.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-write-locale-settings-seam.integration.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-author-display-identity.integration.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/comment-author-display-identity.dogfood.test.ts + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (update-side readonly strip, by-id and multi-row branches, `droppedFields`), packages/objectql/src/validation/rule-validator.ts (`stripReadonlyFields`, `staticReadonlyInsertSubject`, `isPreservableUnderAudit`), packages/objectql/src/engine-execution-plumbing.ts (`buildSession`), packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/index.ts (published exports), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/RecordDetailView.tsx (the console's comment create and edit calls), packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/comment-parent-pair-backfill.ts (the other `sys_comment` writer), content/docs/frontend/plugins/plugin-detail.mdx (the one docs reader of `author_name`)

Face: narrowing (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)` on the PR body and the changeset; no `packages/spec/src/**` path and no governed path in the diff). The net diff against `main` is the eight files of the PR file list; the `.changeset` file is the prose face and is the dispatching seat's ACCEPT.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Create accept set, `sys_comment`, non-system caller with a session — right.** `author_name` and `author_avatar_url` in the request are no longer stored; the create hook assigns both from the session user's own profile after the write is admitted, and assigns them when the request carries neither. The engine's create-side `readonly` strip returns no subject for a `sys_`-prefixed object (`rule-validator.ts`, `staticReadonlyInsertSubject`), so the hook is the only create-side guard, exactly as it already is for `author_id`, `is_edited` and `edited_at`; the integration suite stores the stamped values on a real engine. `sys_comment_reaction` shares the handler and returns before the stamp, so reactions are untouched.
2. **Update accept set, `sys_comment`, non-system caller — right.** Both fields now declare `readonly: true`; the engine's update-side strip runs for every non-system caller (`staticReadonlyStripRuns = !isSystem`) on the by-id branch and on the multi-row branch (a value dropped for one matched row is dropped for all), reports the drop in `droppedFields` and the header, and lands the rest of the write. `hookWrittenKeys` keeps only keys a `beforeUpdate` hook wrote, and no hook writes these two; `preserveAudit` is a server-set import flag. A caller that asks for `strictReadonlyWrites` is refused instead of stripped, which is the engine's standing contract for every `readonly` field, the same as `is_edited` since ruling A on 23124.
3. **System-context writes — right, unchanged.** The comment hook returns before the stamp for `isSystem`, and both strips are skipped for `isSystem`; the integration suite pins a system insert and a system update keeping the values they supply (seeds, imports, the parent-pair backfill, the reactions conversion).
4. **The `@mention` notification title — right.** `writeCommentMentions` names the insert actor from the stored `author_name`, which is now the author's own profile name or none; the editor-not-author case already resolved the editor's snapshot and is unchanged.
5. **Published TypeScript surface of `@objectstack/plugin-audit` — a widening, disclosed, acceptable.** `installAuditWriters` (exported from the entry) returns `AuditWritersHandle | undefined` where it returned `void`; `installCommentAccessHooks` (exported from the entry) takes an optional sixth argument. No existing caller breaks. The four new types (`AuditWritersHandle`, `AuditActorSnapshot`, `CommentAuthorIdentity`, `CommentAuthorIdentityResolver`) are exported from their modules but not re-exported from `index.ts`, the same shape as the existing `AuditWriterOptions`; a host reaches the handle type through `ReturnType` and spells the resolver structurally. Not a must-fix; a one-line re-export would be a courtesy follow-up. The changeset's sentence "Nothing is widened" is exact for the data door and inexact for this composition surface, which the same changeset then names in full under "Hosts that compose the hooks themselves"; the single `(narrowing)` arm is the governing one and is right.
6. **A host that installs the comment hooks without the sixth argument — degrades safely, not silently.** New comments store neither display field, never the request's, and the install logs once at `warn`. Judged against the degradation-level rule: the comment itself is persisted and the missing name is visible to the very next reader (the console shows its unknown-user label), so this is functional, not durability, degradation and `warn` is the right level. The fallback direction is the rule's: the server's value or none.
7. **The console — right, no change needed.** `handleAddComment` still sends `author_name` and `author_avatar_url` on create and they are assigned over with the same user's profile; `handleEditComment` sends `body` and `mentions` only, so an ordinary edit produces no `droppedFields` notice. The one docs example reads `author_name` and is unchanged.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-audit: patch` with the BREAKING banner; `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on the PR body and in the changeset body; the narrowing arm owes the `Skills-docs:` line and the PR body carries it (`none — REASON`). `readonly: true` on two columns of a platform object is a runtime accept-set change, not a change to what a metadata author can write, so `none` is right, and a non-protocol breaking change ships `patch` per the Post-Task Checklist. ADR-0087 disposition: one marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, a category the registration gate carries; nothing stored is read, rewritten or dropped and no authorable spelling or export is retired, so the category is right. `Check Changeset` and the lint gates on this head are green. Level matches what the diff publishes.

### ③ Boundary flags

- PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`: no out-of-relay author to note.
- Acceptance note, "snapshot at creation, at most one profile read per user per 30 s window": answered — it is the same resolution and the same window the record history's actor columns are written with, the console reads the stored `author_name` row by row, and a rename showing on later comments only is what a snapshot is. Accepted.
- Acceptance note, "a host composing the hooks without the resolver stores no display identity and is told once at `warn`": answered in ① item 6. Accepted.
- Not flagged by the PR, judged here: a kernel that composes `AuditPlugin` without the platform's `sys_user` object registered now stores no display name on comments where it used to store the request's, and no warning fires because a resolver is composed. That is the same outcome the `sys_activity` actor columns already have in such a kernel and is the rule's own direction (the server's value or none); accepted, named so the dispatching seat knows it.
- Fixture repair of the locale seam test: the test named its mention actor through a request-carried display name, which the rule now refuses to store; it seeds the author's profile instead and its four assertions are unchanged. Read as evidence the narrowing bites exactly where declared.
- Check-runs on this head, read at 2026-11-03T03:21Z: every completed non-skipped check-run concludes `success`; Test Core (eight shards) and Type Check · workspace were still in progress at the first reading and their final conclusions are reported in the dispatch seat's channel by the reviewer, not assumed here. The landing precondition "all checks green" is the dispatching seat's to read at landing.

### ④ Design judgment

**The rule against the code it cites holds.** The display identity is server-stamped on insert at the same point and in the same manner as `author_id` (session wins, after admission, system exempt), and is frozen on update by the engine's own `readonly` contract rather than by a second hook, so the two fields now have exactly one writer on each path.

**Read-only on update versus re-stamping from the session on update.** The read-only choice is the right one of the two. A comment may be edited by someone who is not its author (a holder of EDIT on the parent record), and `author_id` keeps the creator on such an edit; re-stamping the display fields from the session would then show the editor's name over the author's words, breaking the invariant the PR exists to establish (display identity equals `author_id`'s owner). Read-only keeps the pair bound to the creator on every edit, by the author or by a parent editor, which the integration suite pins. Re-stamping from the author's profile (a refresh) is a different question, declined consistently with the record history's snapshot semantics. The read-only choice also keeps the console's edit call free of `droppedFields` noise.

**Paths tried to break it, each held:** a sessionful caller with no user id stores no display identity, never the request's, because the resolver is only asked for a user id; a resolver that throws or answers a non-string stores none; a context-less bare-kernel call keeps what it is given, as it does for `author_id`, by the same early return; a predicate update over several rows runs the same strip with the all-rows lock; a system insert and a system update keep their values; the profile is read with the system's own read through the hook's `api`, so a caller who cannot read `sys_user` is still named; the one other platform writer of `sys_comment` (the parent-pair backfill) writes in system context and names neither field.

**Tests as evidence:** the new integration suite (real kernel, ObjectQL, AuditPlugin, SQLite, platform `sys_user`) pins the six behaviours, including the dropped-fields report; the new dogfood suite pins the served identity and the PATCH report at the REST data door of a booted stack, with a control that an ordinary comment still shows its caller's own name.

No must-fix.

Implemented-by: `claude/sec-hardening-a`
Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYn5CmmdShCJifm6WYj`

**VERDICT: PASS**
